item.title: What to know after scores were killed in Nigeria while abducted Christians came home
item.description: Gunmen believed to be Islamic extremists killed scores of people in a western Nigerian state that is becoming a new hot spot for the violence that affects large parts of Africa’s most populous country.

item.title: New York’s incoming archbishop will focus on evangelizing and reengagement
item.description: The incoming archbishop of New York said Thursday that he plans to emphasize the importance of evangelizing as he takes charge of one of the biggest U.S. archdioceses.

item.title: Pope, an avid athlete, extols physical and spiritual benefits of sport in Olympic message
item.description: Pope Leo XIV, an avid tennis player and sports fan, marked the start of the Winter Games on Friday by extolling the positive values of sport and fair play while warning that the pursuit of profits and performance risked corrupting sport entirely.

item.title: In a Nigerian village, extremists issued a call to prayer and then slaughtered those who turned up
item.description: Weeks after residents of two Nigerian villages ignored a letter from militants announcing they would come to spread their extreme form of Islam, gunmen arrived on motorbikes and embarked on a 10-hour frenzy of killing.

item.title: Architect aims to rebuild a church and help restore a quake-hit Turkish city’s multicultural past
item.description: ANTAKYA, Turkey — Architect Buse Ceren Gul is on a mission: restore a 166-year-old Greek Orthodox church that was long a beacon of her hometown’s multicultural past. She believes restoring the church left mostly in ruins by the earthquakes in southern Turkey three years ago will help locals reconnect to their […]

item.title: Mozambique Archbishop blames dam management for catastrophic floods
item.description: In Mozambique, when the Búzi River surged to a devastating 40 feet above sea level this January, it unleashed a torrent of floodwaters that swallowed homes, cut off entire communities, and left thousands homeless.

item.title: African theologians decry ‘troubling pattern’ of human rights abuses in Uganda
item.description: Catholic theologians from PACTPAN have complained about the shrinking democratic space in Uganda following the recent crackdown on protesters, including the arrest of a Catholic priest, Father Deusdedit Ssekabira.

item.title: Pope receives Courage International leadership delegation
item.description: Courage International called the audience a “momentous occasion” and said it “affirms the peaceful joy of the staff and members of Courage who seek to grow in holiness through living the truth in love.”

item.title: New Catholic archbishop of New York wants a church that ‘shows respect for all’ and builds unity
item.description: Ronald Hicks was installed Friday as the 11th archbishop of New York in a ceremony at the revered St. Patrick’s Cathedral in Manhattan, calling on Catholics to spread the faith while respecting all people and helping the vulnerable.

item.title: Comments from outgoing CBCI president criticized by lay leadership group, turned into parting shot by conference
item.description: Bishop Andrews Thazhath, the leader of a major Syro-Malabar jurisdiction and the first Syro-Malabar prelate to have served as president of the Indian bishops’ conference, was replaced in a CBCI vote on Saturday.
